EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong C=C band at 1648 cm⁻¹, high-frequency =C–H stretches at 3022 and 3090 cm⁻¹, and the characteristic pair of =CH₂ out-of-plane deformation bands at ~999 and ~923 cm⁻¹, all indicating a terminal alkene. Multiple CH stretches centered at 2873–2990 cm⁻¹ and CH deformations at 1458/1424 cm⁻¹ fit an alkyl substituent (isopropyl). Notably, there is no clear O–H or N–H stretch near 3300–3500 cm⁻¹, disfavoring candidates with OH/NH (e.g., 1, 3, 2). The broad band near 1094 cm⁻¹ and the feature at 1247 cm⁻¹ are consistent with C–O–C stretching in an ether. Overall, these features best match a vinyl ether, supporting candidate 6 (C=COCC(C)C).
